_comment: GENERATED by tools/rituals-plain-text.mjs from tools/data/ritual-plain-text.json. Read at runtime by scripts/ritual-seal.mjs so a sealed Working card carries the same plain-language block as its Formula Item. Do not edit by hand.

Ward the Room.story: You walk the edges of one room laying a line of blessed salt along the threshold and burning resin in the corners until the air goes still. Anything on the other side of the Veil that tries to lean in finds the room hard to look at.
Ward the Room.plain: Ghosts, spirits and any magic aimed into the room from outside get a bane — one penalty die on the roll. It does not stop people, bullets, cameras or hackers at all.
Ward the Room.magnitude: Magnitude 1 is the smallest Working there is: one room, one night, one bane. Bigger wards in this family cover more ground, last longer, or hit harder.
Ward the Room.scope: One room. Only Veil things — spirits and magic. Sprites, Agents, ICE and Wire snooping walk straight through it; for those, lay Data Ward.
Ward the Room.seal: One evening's work and one roll at the end. Low: it hangs — the Director holds a half-finished ward that may go off wrong. Middle: the ward is up. High: the ward is up and the cost of making it is blunted one step.
Ward the Room.expires: At the next dawn (or the next dusk, if you sealed it at night — pick when you seal). Breaking the salt line ends it early.

Seal the Flat.story: Three nights of work: salt at every door, chalk on every window, a mark scratched into each vent. When it is done the whole place feels like somebody is awake in it, even when nobody is.
Seal the Flat.plain: Every room, door, window and vent of one dwelling gets the same bane Ward the Room gives one room. The first time something Veil-side forces its way in, you wake up and know, wherever you are in the district.
Seal the Flat.magnitude: Magnitude 2 buys the whole flat instead of one room, plus the alarm. It also means you need a sanctum rated 2 to seal it.
Seal the Flat.scope: One dwelling, up to about six rooms — a Flats unit, a safehouse floor, a coffin-cube row. Veil only; for the flat's node lay Data Ward as well.
Seal the Flat.seal: This card runs study, sanctum and sealing all as Projects — it is the worked example of the full chain. Low: hung, and the flat is not sealed. Middle: sealed. High: sealed, and one step of Price is blunted.
Seal the Flat.expires: At the third dawn after sealing. Re-lay the thresholds before then (¥60 of salt, one evening, no roll) for three more dawns. Miss a renewal and it lapses — you start again at sealing, not at the beginning.

Street-Focus Charm.story: You spend a night rubbing a stain, a sheen or a varnish into something you already carry — a focus, a knife, a deck — until it stops being just yours and starts being part of the work.
Street-Focus Charm.plain: One named magic (or Resonance) ability gets an edge — one bonus die — whenever you use it through that item. Or, instead, the item picks up one Veil tag for the run.
Street-Focus Charm.magnitude: Magnitude 2 is charm-tier and that is the ceiling: there is no permanent version of this card. For a permanent implement you want Telesma Birth.
Street-Focus Charm.scope: One item you already own, and one ability named when you seal it. It never gives you an ability you did not have.
Street-Focus Charm.seal: One evening. Low: hung — no charm. Middle: the charm holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted one step.
Street-Focus Charm.expires: At the end of the session, or at your next major respite — the Director picks which when you seal it.

Remote Sense.story: You sit still with your eyes shut and borrow somebody else's. A jacked-in friend, a tagged camera, a small spirit perched on a ledge — whatever is out there looking, you look through it.
Remote Sense.plain: For one scene you see and hear whatever your spotter sees and hears, at any distance inside the printed Reach or Wired range.
Remote Sense.magnitude: Magnitude 2 is a one-scene borrow through a spotter who is already there. Reaching a target with no spotter needs a link Working (Hair-and-Wire, Keepsake, Effigy) on top.
Remote Sense.scope: You need a spotter at the far end. The link runs both ways: it can be traced back to you, and a bad seal or a won trace can reverse the pipe for a round — meaning they see you.
Remote Sense.seal: One evening. Low: hung, or the pipe points the wrong way. Middle: you get the scene. High: the scene, and Price blunted one step.
Remote Sense.expires: At the end of the scene, or the moment the link is cut — the spotter is knocked out, the camera dies, the trace wins.

Watcher.story: You call something small and patient and give it one job: sit here and tell me. It nests in a stairwell or a camera housing and does not move.
Watcher.plain: A minor spirit or daemon guards a place you mark. When the condition you set is met, it tells you — once — and then waits for orders or fades. It never blocks or fights anything.
Watcher.magnitude: Magnitude 2 buys one small watcher and one warning. To get something that guards a place permanently you want Site Bind (Magnitude 4).
Watcher.scope: The marked site only. A Veil watcher sees spirits and people; a Wire daemon-watcher sees the node and its cameras. Neither one is a wall.
Watcher.seal: One evening. Low: hung — nothing arrives, or something arrives you did not ask for. Middle: the watcher is on post. High: on post, and Price blunted one step.
Watcher.expires: After hours equal to 4 × Persona (Street Priest) or 4 × Logic (Elementalist, Technomancer), or the moment you dismiss it.

Site Bind.story: You speak a name you were not supposed to learn, and something agrees to live in the walls. It knows every floorboard now. It was not asked politely.
Site Bind.plain: A named spirit, elemental or Wire-entity becomes the permanent guardian of a sanctum you have built. You must already know its name — from study, from Discover Lore, or from meeting it.
Site Bind.magnitude: Magnitude 4 is heavy: it wants a sanctum rated 4, a night of sealing, and it moves faction clocks. Anyone Unmaking it has to beat Magnitude 4 and go through you.
Site Bind.scope: It guards the site and nothing else. It does not come with you on a run unless your copy of the Formula says so. A Wire-entity guards the node side; a spirit guards the Veil side.
Site Bind.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and a named power now knows who called it. Middle: it is bound. High: bound, and Price blunted one step.
Site Bind.expires: It does not — while the sanctum keystone stands and you keep paying the favour you owe. Break the keystone and it goes. Stop paying and the leash slips, which feeds Incursion and hands the Director Malice.

Circle of Many.story: Chalk stations on the floor, one body at each of them, and a chant nobody in the room is good enough to carry alone.
Circle of Many.plain: This does nothing by itself. It supports a different Working: every assistant station turns into an edge on that Working's sealing roll, or into extra Project progress toward it. A very big circle may let the Director raise one sealing's Magnitude ceiling by 1.
Circle of Many.magnitude: Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 2 and 4. The higher it is, the more stations it can hold and the more heat it draws.
Circle of Many.scope: It only ever helps another card. Non-casters can hold stations, which is the point — the whole crew can be in this one.
Circle of Many.seal: The circle is sealed as part of the night it supports. Low: a station fails and the circle fights the Working. Middle: the edges land. High: the edges land and Price is blunted a step.
Circle of Many.expires: At the end of the sealing night or Project block it was built for. The chalk marks stay on the floor until somebody cleans them.

Exclusive Charter Rite.story: A lodge writes its own name into its Formulas, so that a stolen copy reads like a recipe with the verbs missing.
Exclusive Charter Rite.plain: One Working — or a small list of them — can only be led and sealed by members of your charter. Anyone outside it takes a bane on the sealing roll, and stolen copies go blurry in their hands.
Exclusive Charter Rite.magnitude: Magnitude 3 sets the strength of the lock: Unmaking it needs Magnitude 3 or better.
Exclusive Charter Rite.scope: It governs who may use the chartered Formulas. It does not protect the physical book from being taken — only from being useful.
Exclusive Charter Rite.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and the charter is readable by anyone until you try again. Middle: locked. High: locked, Price blunted a step.
Exclusive Charter Rite.expires: Never, on its own. It ends when the charter is dissolved, Unmade, or when its living keys — the members whose names are in it — are all dead.

Lodge Keystone.story: A stone, a server rack or a beam gets carved, blessed and bolted in place, and the building around it stops being rented rooms and starts being yours.
Lodge Keystone.plain: Your shared workspace becomes a permanent sanctum and its rating goes up by 1, to a maximum of 3 without further Projects. Sanctum rating is the gate on what Magnitude you are allowed to seal there. If your copy says so, the inside also gets a light ward — a bane on hostile spirits and magic peeks.
Lodge Keystone.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. Unmaking it has to beat the lodge's current rating, not the card's Magnitude.
Lodge Keystone.scope: Veil only. The ward-lite does nothing against Wire intrusion — lay Data Ward for that. Your Lifestyle band caps how high a rating the address can hold, whatever you spend.
Lodge Keystone.seal: A night's work, and a permanent ¥ upkeep after it. Low: hung — the keystone is inert stone. Middle: the rating goes up. High: the rating goes up and Price is blunted a step.
Lodge Keystone.expires: Never, while you pay the Lifestyle upkeep. Stop paying, or destroy the keystone, and the rating goes with it.

Hair-and-Wire Link.story: You need a piece of them. Hair, blood, a shard of a god-file, the core out of a deep handle. It is cold work and half the Reach will arrest you for it.
Hair-and-Wire Link.plain: Lets you aim a Reach Working at somebody with nobody standing near them. The remnant is the aim.
Hair-and-Wire Link.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3; the higher one reaches further and holds against a better-defended target.
Hair-and-Wire Link.scope: Blood and tissue aim Veil Workings; handle cores and god-file shards aim Wire-rites. This leaves a much louder trace than Remote Sense through a live spotter, and a fake remnant fouls the seal — a bane, or backlash.
Hair-and-Wire Link.seal: One evening, spent as part of the Working it aims. Low: the aim is wrong, or it points home. Middle: the aim holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Hair-and-Wire Link.expires: It powers exactly one following Reach sealing or scene, then it is spent. Destroying the remnant ends it early.

Keepsake Link.story: Not blood — a letter, a ring, a child's shoe, an archive nobody else kept. Things people love remember them.
Keepsake Link.plain: Aims a Reach Working through something the target treasures, when you cannot get anything off their body. Weaker than flesh and harder to seal, but it leaves an emotional trail anyone sensitive can follow.
Keepsake Link.magnitude: Magnitude 3 — one step harder than Hair-and-Wire, because love is a worse aim than blood.
Keepsake Link.scope: One Reach payoff scene. Traceable like every Reach link: they can follow it back to you.
Keepsake Link.seal: One night. Low: hung, and the keepsake may be ruined. Middle: the aim holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Keepsake Link.expires: After one Reach payoff scene. Returning or destroying the keepsake ends it immediately.

Effigy Link.story: You build a small ugly version of the thing you mean to reach — a doll, a model of the flat, a double drawn in glyphs — and then you do to the model what you cannot get close enough to do for real.
Effigy Link.plain: A stand-in that lets you aim a Reach or Unmaking Working across distance when you have no remnant and no keepsake. Scaffolding for the big remote Workings.
Effigy Link.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. A Magnitude 4 build is loud enough that faction clocks move just because you made it.
Effigy Link.scope: It aims other Workings; on its own it does nothing. Unmaking the link needs a Magnitude at least equal to the link's.
Effigy Link.seal: A night's craft. Low: the effigy is wrong and the Working it aims goes wrong with it. Middle: it aims true. High: it aims true and Price is blunted a step.
Effigy Link.expires: When it is spent on a sealing, or when somebody burns it.

Door-Seal Glyph.story: One glyph, cut into one door frame, small enough to miss. Spirits go around. So does the Wire.
Door-Seal Glyph.plain: That single doorway refuses spirits, magic peeks and Wire bleed. It does nothing to flesh or bullets — those still only have to deal with the wood and the hinges.
Door-Seal Glyph.magnitude: Magnitude 2. Unmaking it needs Magnitude 2. Its strength is that it covers both sides — Veil and Wire — for a Magnitude that only buys one side elsewhere.
Door-Seal Glyph.scope: That one doorway. Walls, vents and every other door in the building are wide open.
Door-Seal Glyph.seal: One evening. Low: hung — the glyph is a scratch. Middle: the door is sealed. High: sealed, Price blunted a step.
Door-Seal Glyph.expires: When it is broken or Unmade, or at the expiry your copy prints — usually a number of dawns equal to its Magnitude, or for as long as you keep paying sanctum upkeep.

Charged Perimeter.story: A ward that has been holding its breath. It does nothing at all until the wrong thing steps over the line, and then it lets go all at once.
Charged Perimeter.plain: A silent ward that stores power and spends it in one go when it is crossed. What it does when it goes off is printed on your copy: a scream of an alarm, a stun pulse, a Malice tick, or some combination.
Charged Perimeter.magnitude: Magnitude 3 sets how hard it hits and what it takes to Unmake it. It is also loud enough to detect from further away than Ward the Room.
Charged Perimeter.scope: The perimeter you walked. Your copy names what trips it — spirits, magic peeks, named people, or (with the ICE-capacitor build) Wire intrusion.
Charged Perimeter.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — it may fire at the wrong thing, at the wrong time. Middle: it is armed. High: armed, and Price blunted a step.
Charged Perimeter.expires: The moment it discharges — once. Keep it charged instead with sanctum upkeep, paid in ¥ and reagents; it never costs a pool.

Reagent Still.story: A still in the back room, three days of dripping, and one small sealed pack of something that smells like a church and a battery at the same time.
Reagent Still.plain: Makes a single-use reagent pack. Spend it at a later sealing and that sealing gets an edge, or its Price is blunted once — your call when you spend it.
Reagent Still.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 1 or 2; the Magnitude 2 version makes a stronger pack (your copy prints which).
Reagent Still.scope: It helps one later sealing. The pack is a separate item on the sheet — it can be stolen like anything else.
Reagent Still.seal: An evening. Low: hung, and the batch is spoiled. Middle: you get a pack. High: a pack, and Price blunted a step.
Reagent Still.expires: The pack lasts until it is used or until it spoils — usually one season or three sessions, printed on your copy.

True Relic Carve.story: Months of work on one object, and at the end of it you own something that has never existed before and that somebody will eventually kill you for.
True Relic Carve.plain: Carves a permanent prototype relic — a Restricted-or-better item with unique flags written by the Director. This is campaign gravity, not shopping. The Director can say no.
True Relic Carve.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. Magnitude 5 means the whole hive whispers about it: everybody with an ear in the Veil knows something was made.
True Relic Carve.scope: The relic's own printed flags say whether it touches the Veil, the Wire, or both. Unbonding it needs Magnitude 4–5.
True Relic Carve.seal: A night or a short climax scene. Low: hung, and a half-made relic is a liability. Middle: the relic exists. High: it exists and Price is blunted a step.
True Relic Carve.expires: Never. It ends when it is destroyed, unbonded, corrupted, or when the doom clock printed on the relic itself runs out.

Long Leash.story: Not a summoning — a contract. Something you already called agrees to keep doing small jobs for a while, and a tablet on your wall keeps the schedule.
Long Leash.plain: Binds an entity you have already called to intermittent services over days or weeks: carrying messages, standing watch, whispering, one dirty job. It does not mean "it fights beside me this round".
Long Leash.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. The higher copy holds a stronger entity and for longer.
Long Leash.scope: Veil spirits and elementals. A Technomancer leading the Wire version should use Daemon Long Leash instead.
Long Leash.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and the entity is loose and annoyed. Middle: the leash holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Long Leash.expires: After the days or weeks you sealed it for. Renew it with another favour before then, or it lapses. Breaking the schedule tablet ends it at once.

True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).story: You say the name it was given before the world had people in it, and it stops. This is the card that gets characters killed.
True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).plain: Collars an unbound named power — one nobody else has leashed — by its secret name or its deep handle. The Price is high and your copy prints the exact conditions under which it gets loose again.
True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. Magnitude 5 moves faction clocks whether you wanted that or not.
True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).scope: Name-based. A true name collars a Veil power; a deep handle collars a Wire power (Technomancers have their own card, True-Handle Collar). It is contested by the thing you are collaring.
True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: hung — and it now knows your name too. Middle: collared. High: collared, Price blunted a step.
True-Name Collar (Deep Bind).expires: When one of the escape conditions printed on your copy is met, when somebody Unmakes it at Magnitude 4–5, or when you die.

Vessel Dressing.story: You prepare a body, a drone shell or a statue the way an undertaker prepares a room: washed, marked, and made ready for a guest.
Vessel Dressing.plain: Makes something a legal vessel for a called entity to wear. Without it, possession is messy, hostile, or fatal to whoever is inside.
Vessel Dressing.magnitude: Magnitude 3. Unmaking the dressing — spoiling it before the guest arrives — needs Magnitude 3.
Vessel Dressing.scope: It enables clean possession, drone-rides and idol-walks for a later Calling. It does not call anything itself. The Technomancer version for Wire-entities is Chassis Dressing.
Vessel Dressing.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and the vessel is a hazard. Middle: dressed and ready. High: ready, Price blunted a step.
Vessel Dressing.expires: When it is inhabited, or when the dressing spoils — usually days equal to its Magnitude, printed on your copy.

Great Circle.story: Everyone you trust, in one room, for one night, doing something none of you are supposed to be able to do.
Great Circle.plain: With an initiate-grade leader and a full circle, one sealing may exceed the normal Magnitude cap by 1. It is a campaign lever, and it is easy to regret pulling it.
Great Circle.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, which is also what the circle itself costs in sanctum and study before it helps anything.
Great Circle.scope: It supports another Working. On its own it does nothing except attract attention across the whole hive.
Great Circle.seal: One night. Low: the circle breaks and the Working it supports goes wrong. Middle: the ceiling lifts. High: the ceiling lifts and Price is blunted a step.
Great Circle.expires: It empowers exactly one sealing night, then it is over.

Scrub the Stain.story: Scrubbing is the honest word. It takes hours, it hurts, and at the end the mark is gone or it is not.
Scrub the Stain.plain: Strips a hung curse, a toxic mark, corrupted ward residue, or Taint (the cleanse ladder is in chapter 27). If the seal only half-works you still push the stain one step down its clock.
Scrub the Stain.magnitude: This card's Magnitude must be equal to or greater than the stain you are scrubbing. Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 1 and 5, and that number is the ceiling on what it can clean.
Scrub the Stain.scope: Veil stains. Corrupted code, Overlay marks and hung daemons need Scrub the Ghost-Code instead.
Scrub the Stain.seal: One evening or one night, depending on the copy's Magnitude. Low: partial — one clock step. Middle: the stain is gone. High: gone, and Price blunted a step.
Scrub the Stain.expires: Immediately — the effect is instant at a successful sealing. There is nothing left standing to expire.

Detox Domain.story: A whole block is sick. You go into the sick part of it and argue with what is making it sick, for a night, out loud.
Detox Domain.plain: Pushes a toxic thin-place's agenda clock back one step. A failure makes the stain worse instead.
Detox Domain.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, and it must be equal to or greater than the domain's stain or it cannot touch it.
Detox Domain.scope: Veil toxicity across a site. Wire-poisoned nodes need Scrub the Ghost-Code, at scale.
Detox Domain.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: the stain deepens. Middle: the clock goes back one. High: back one, and Price blunted a step.
Detox Domain.expires: Instantly — it is a single clock move, not a standing effect. The domain pushes back on its next tick.

Thin-Path.story: Two places where the world is worn thin, and one night where you convince them they are the same place. You walk through, and the door shuts behind you.
Thin-Path.plain: Opens a short path between two thin places you already know, big enough for the crew to walk through once.
Thin-Path.magnitude: Magnitude 3 buys one crew-sized crossing between known anchors. It also needs a sanctum rated 3 to seal.
Thin-Path.scope: Veil only, and both ends must be thin places you have studied or visited. The district notices automatically — Concord and corp clocks advance on any Magnitude 3+ Threshold Working in the Reach.
Thin-Path.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — the path opens somewhere you did not choose, or not at all. Middle: it opens. High: it opens and Price is blunted a step.
Thin-Path.expires: It collapses the moment the last of you is through. Either end can also be collapsed from outside with an Unmaking at Magnitude 3 or better.

Domain Aspect.story: By morning it is raining ash on four streets and nowhere else, and the ash is not from anything burning.
Domain Aspect.plain: Paints Veil weather over a block for a session — ash rain, static bloom, soft gravity, whatever your element is. Things that match the weather get an edge; things opposed to it get a bane.
Domain Aspect.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. The higher copy covers more ground and is harder to Unmake.
Domain Aspect.scope: Veil only, over one block. Civilians feel it and talk about it, and the opposition will plan around it — this is not subtle.
Domain Aspect.seal: A night's work. Low: the weather comes, wrong, and possibly on you. Middle: the block changes. High: it changes and Price is blunted a step.
Domain Aspect.expires: At the end of the session, or after two dawns — your copy picks which. An opposing Domain Aspect cancels it early.

Invoke Greater Shape.story: You do not summon this. You invite it, and then you spend the whole scene being the reason it has not turned around.
Invoke Greater Shape.plain: Calls a greater-shape elemental for one climax scene. This is the "we brought a disaster on a leash" button.
Invoke Greater Shape.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. Both spike Price and Malice; Magnitude 5 hands the Director a great deal of both.
Invoke Greater Shape.scope: A set-piece summon for one scene, not a servant for downtime — for that, use Long Leash. It is contested if anybody tries to banish it.
Invoke Greater Shape.seal: A night or the climax scene itself. Low: it arrives unbound. Middle: it arrives on the leash. High: on the leash, and Price blunted a step.
Invoke Greater Shape.expires: At the end of the climax scene or encounter. Then it leaves — or, if the leash failed, it unbinds violently on the way out.

Anchor Rune.story: A rune cut into a floorboard, a lintel or the underside of a table, holding one spell still until somebody walks into it.
Anchor Rune.plain: Stores one magic ability you already know and fires it on a trigger you write when you seal it — when the door opens, when the room is empty, when I stop breathing. Then the rune is spent.
Anchor Rune.magnitude: Magnitude 3. Unmaking or disarming it needs Magnitude 3, or a disarm scene at the table.
Anchor Rune.scope: The ability has to be one the leader actually knows — this stores a spell, it does not invent one. Veil only.
Anchor Rune.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — the rune may fire early, or at you. Middle: it is set. High: set, and Price blunted a step.
Anchor Rune.expires: When it triggers, or when it spoils — usually at the end of the session or at your next respite, printed on your copy. Scraping the rune ends it.

Telesma Birth.story: You do not decorate something you own. You make the thing from scratch, out of prepared matter, over weeks, and at the end it is an implement and not an object.
Telesma Birth.plain: Creates or upgrades a tradition focus from prepared telesma. The result is a new focus item on your sheet. This is building an implement; Street-Focus Charm is only dressing one you already have.
Telesma Birth.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. The Magnitude 3 version makes a better focus and takes a bigger sanctum.
Telesma Birth.scope: Elementalist tradition gear only, and it still obeys the signature-focus bond limit in chapter 8 — making two does not let you benefit from two.
Telesma Birth.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and the telesma is wasted. Middle: the focus exists. High: it exists and Price is blunted a step.
Telesma Birth.expires: Never. It ends when the focus is shattered or unbonded (Unmaking at Magnitude 2–3).

Storm Ward.story: The ward has an element in it, and it has opinions. A fire-ward hates water ghosts. A stone-ward hates anything that flies.
Storm Ward.plain: An element-aspected barrier. It gives the usual ward bane to everything Veil-side, and bites the opposite element or spirit type particularly hard.
Storm Ward.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. The higher copy covers more ground and bites harder.
Storm Ward.scope: Veil only. It does nothing against Wire intrusion — use Data Ward for that.
Storm Ward.seal: An evening or a night, by Magnitude. Low: hung, and the element may turn on the room. Middle: the ward is up. High: up, and Price blunted a step.
Storm Ward.expires: As printed on your copy — at the next dawn, at the end of the session, or for as long as you keep paying sanctum upkeep.

Nest Claim.story: The roaches in this building work for you now. So do the moths, and whatever is living in the riser. They all look the same way at the same time and it is deeply unpleasant to watch.
Nest Claim.plain: Claims a nest — vermin or small elementals — as a living alarm across a small site. Many tiny watchers, run as one Working.
Nest Claim.magnitude: Magnitude 3. Unmaking the claim needs Magnitude 3; burning the nest does it for free.
Nest Claim.scope: It watches with Veil senses and with ordinary eyes; it does not block anything. Civilians in the building notice and complain about "bugs that stare".
Nest Claim.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — the nest is hostile, or simply leaves. Middle: the lattice is live. High: live, and Price blunted a step.
Nest Claim.expires: After days equal to your Logic, or the moment the nest burns.

Hive Crack.story: There is one stone holding the whole infestation together. You find it, you spend a night talking it apart, and then the building sighs.
Hive Crack.plain: Collapses the keystone of a nest-sanctum that serves a hive or infestation. The place comes apart structurally and spiritually at once.
Hive Crack.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, and it has to be at least equal to what it is breaking.
Hive Crack.scope: You need to know where the keystone actually is. Expect to pay for that knowledge with a fight.
Hive Crack.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: you tip it off, and it moves the keystone. Middle: it collapses. High: it collapses and Price is blunted a step.
Hive Crack.expires: Instantly — the collapse is the payoff. The aftermath clocks linger, and the hive will build a new keystone somewhere else.

Consecrated Thin-Path.story: The same crossing the Elementalists make, but it only works on ground somebody has prayed over, and the trip tastes of your pact the whole way.
Consecrated Thin-Path.plain: Opens a short path between two thin places for one crew crossing, but only from consecrated ground. It costs the travellers less than the Elementalist version does, and Light or Dark pact flavour stains the crossing.
Consecrated Thin-Path.magnitude: Magnitude 3, the same as Thin-Path, and it needs a sanctum rated 3.
Consecrated Thin-Path.scope: Veil Threshold, consecrated ends only. It draws the same notice and the same heat as Thin-Path — the district knows.
Consecrated Thin-Path.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — the path does not open, or opens on the wrong ground. Middle: it opens. High: it opens and Price is blunted a step.
Consecrated Thin-Path.expires: As soon as the crew is through. Desecrating either end collapses it.

Pact Charter.story: Terms, written out, signed by everyone. Keep them and the work gets easier. Break them and you find out what the other party thought signing meant.
Pact Charter.plain: Binds the crew to Light or Dark terms. While you keep them, later Workings get edges on their sealing rolls. Break them and you take backlash.
Pact Charter.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. The higher copy binds harder and gives a bigger edge — and a worse backlash.
Pact Charter.scope: It binds the people who signed it. This is crew identity written down as rules.
Pact Charter.seal: An evening or a night. Low: hung, and the terms bind without the benefit. Middle: the charter holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Pact Charter.expires: Never on its own. It ends when the terms are broken, when the charter is rewritten, when somebody Unmakes it, or in a mutual release scene.

Ally Heart.story: You do not call this one and send it away. You make it a heart, and it stays, and it is on the crew sheet with a name.
Ally Heart.plain: Forges a long-term ally companion spirit with a short list of powers and an ongoing favour-debt you have to keep paying. This is a named member of the crew, not a disposable Watcher.
Ally Heart.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5. The Magnitude 5 version supports a stronger power list.
Ally Heart.scope: A Veil spirit. It does not replace your Invoke the Pact uses unless the Director builds a bridge for that.
Ally Heart.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: hung, and something answers that is not an ally. Middle: the ally exists. High: it exists and Price is blunted a step.
Ally Heart.expires: It lasts the campaign while the favour-debt is honoured. It ends on a failed Ally Reforge, on an Unmaking at Magnitude 4–5, or the day you betray the terms.

Ally Reforge.story: You open the ally up and change something about what it is. It agreed to this. It still hurts.
Ally Reforge.plain: Adds or swaps one power on an Ally Heart you already have. If the seal fails, the bond fractures: the ally is hurt, gone, or hostile for a clock.
Ally Reforge.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4. It must be at least as strong as the power you are trying to add.
Ally Reforge.scope: It needs an existing Ally Heart to work on. It cannot make one.
Ally Reforge.seal: A night's work — and this card's failure is unusually harsh, because there is no counter to it except getting the roll right. Low: the bond fractures. Middle: the power changes. High: it changes and Price is blunted a step.
Ally Reforge.expires: Instantly — the change is permanent, and the ally's own duration is untouched.

Exorcist's Unmaking.story: A kind voice, a steady hand on the forehead, and a boot behind the door. Something comes out of them, and what is left may not be a person any more.
Exorcist's Unmaking.plain: Tears a possessing entity out of a body or a site. The vessel may not survive it.
Exorcist's Unmaking.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4, and it must be at least as strong as the thing possessing the vessel.
Exorcist's Unmaking.scope: Veil possessors. A Wire-entity riding somebody's chrome needs Scrub the Ghost-Code instead. Knowing the possessor's true name gives you an edge.
Exorcist's Unmaking.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: the possession gets worse, and the possessor knows you now. Middle: it comes out. High: it comes out and Price is blunted a step.
Exorcist's Unmaking.expires: Instantly — possession ends at a successful sealing. There is nothing standing to expire.

Blood-Price Refusal.story: Somebody else is halfway through a sacrifice. You kick the altar over during the hymn. They will never forget you did it.
Blood-Price Refusal.plain: Spoils a rival sealing that is being paid for in blood, while it is happening. Enormous heat; permanent enemies.
Blood-Price Refusal.magnitude: Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 3 and 5, and it must be equal to or greater than the rival Working's or it simply fails.
Blood-Price Refusal.scope: Rival sacrifice-fuelled Workings only. This is an interrupt, not a ward.
Blood-Price Refusal.seal: Resolved in the scene, against their roll. Low: you are outmatched and they finish. Middle: the rival Working is spoiled, or one of its clock steps is. High: spoiled, and your own Price blunted a step.
Blood-Price Refusal.expires: Instantly — it spoils one Working or one clock step, and then it is over.

Confession Ward.story: A threshold that knows who is lying. The faithful walk over it without noticing. Anybody carrying something they will not say out loud hesitates, and everyone sees them do it.
Confession Ward.plain: A faith-keyed barrier: allies of your pact cross with an edge, anyone opposed to it takes a bane, and liars flinch visibly at the line.
Confession Ward.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 1 or 2. The Magnitude 2 version covers a larger threshold and is harder to Unmake.
Confession Ward.scope: Veil and pact only. It does nothing against Wire intrusion — use Data Ward for that.
Confession Ward.seal: An evening. Low: hung, and the ward may read your own crew as opposed. Middle: it is up. High: up, and Price blunted a step.
Confession Ward.expires: At the next dawn, or for as long as you keep paying sanctum upkeep.

Uncrook the Path.story: Somebody's ministry has been bent into a shape it was not supposed to take. You spend a night straightening it, and what is holding the bend looks back at you.
Uncrook the Path.plain: Breaks a rival Working belonging to a twisted or corrupted tradition. Doing it may reveal who is actually behind the crooked ministry.
Uncrook the Path.magnitude: Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 3 and 5, and it must be equal to or greater than the Working you are breaking.
Uncrook the Path.scope: Corrupted tradition Workings. It is contested by the ministry that laid it.
Uncrook the Path.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: it holds, and they know. Middle: it breaks. High: it breaks and Price is blunted a step.
Uncrook the Path.expires: Instantly against the target Working. The revelation clocks it starts run on afterwards.

Data Ward.story: Chalk, but the chalk is conductive, and the circle is a Faraday cage with a prayer in the earth strap.
Data Ward.plain: The Wire's version of Ward the Room. Sprites, Agents, ICE and Overlay intrusion into the caged volume all take a bane. A Magnitude 2 copy also covers magic peeks.
Data Ward.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 1 or 2. Magnitude 1 stops Wire things only; Magnitude 2 stops Wire things and magic peeks. Neither one stops spirits — for those, lay Ward the Room too.
Data Ward.scope: One node, flat or server closet. It is a volume, not a doorway.
Data Ward.seal: An evening. Low: hung — the cage is decorative. Middle: the cage is live. High: live, and Price blunted a step.
Data Ward.expires: When the node reboots, at the next dawn, or the moment the cage is physically broken.

Signal Charm.story: A night with the deck open and your hands inside it, writing something into the firmware that is not code.
Signal Charm.plain: Short-bonds a deck or focus so that one named Resonance or magic ability gets an edge through it for the session.
Signal Charm.magnitude: Magnitude 2 — the same tier as Street-Focus Charm, which is its Veil twin. Unbonding it needs Magnitude 2.
Signal Charm.scope: One deck or focus, one named ability. It never gives you an ability you did not have.
Signal Charm.seal: An evening. Low: hung, and the deck may be worse than it was. Middle: the charm holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Signal Charm.expires: At the end of the session. Wiping the deck ends it early.

Deep Overlay Sense.story: You ride somebody else's eyes through the Overlay — a jacked-in friend, or forty cameras you do not own.
Deep Overlay Sense.plain: For one scene you perceive through a jacked-in ally or a compromised camera swarm. Remote Sense, built Overlay-native.
Deep Overlay Sense.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 2 or 3. The higher copy reaches deeper and resists the trace better.
Deep Overlay Sense.scope: Wire Reach only. It is traceable, and a failed seal risks the trace coming home to you.
Deep Overlay Sense.seal: An evening or a night. Low: hung, or traced. Middle: you get the scene. High: the scene, and Price blunted a step.
Deep Overlay Sense.expires: At the end of the scene, or when the feeds are killed.

Daemon Long Leash.story: A sandbox in the corner of your rig with something living in it that answers when you knock, and does jobs while you sleep.
Daemon Long Leash.plain: Long-term bind of a Wire-entity for intermittent downtime services: crawler jobs, watching a node, whispering through cameras. A digital familiar on contract — not Compile Sprite spam.
Daemon Long Leash.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 3 or 4; the higher copy holds a stronger entity for longer.
Daemon Long Leash.scope: Wire-entities only. The Veil version of this card is Long Leash.
Daemon Long Leash.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and something is loose in your rig. Middle: the leash holds. High: it holds and Price is blunted a step.
Daemon Long Leash.expires: After the days or weeks you sealed it for — renew it or it lapses. Wiping the sandbox ends it immediately, and so does the escape clause printed on your copy.

True-Handle Collar.story: Deep Bind for deck jockeys who think they are immortal. You have the handle. You say it. It stops moving.
True-Handle Collar.plain: Collars an unbound Wire power by its secret handle. If it gets loose, that escape feeds Incursion.
True-Handle Collar.magnitude: Your copy is written at Magnitude 4 or 5, and Magnitude 5 moves faction clocks on its own.
True-Handle Collar.scope: Wire powers only. The Veil version is True-Name Collar.
True-Handle Collar.seal: A night or a climax scene. Low: hung — and it has your handle now. Middle: collared. High: collared, and Price blunted a step.
True-Handle Collar.expires: When the escape printed on your copy happens, when the handle leaks, or when somebody wipes or Unmakes it at Magnitude 4–5.

Chassis Dressing.story: You prepare an empty drone the way an undertaker prepares a room, except the guest is made of signal and the room has wheels.
Chassis Dressing.plain: Prepares a drone or empty chrome as a legal vessel for a called Wire-entity. Vessel Dressing, Wire skin.
Chassis Dressing.magnitude: Magnitude 3, the same as its Veil twin. Spoiling the dressing needs Magnitude 3.
Chassis Dressing.scope: Wire-entities only. It prepares the vessel; it does not call the guest.
Chassis Dressing.seal: A night's work. Low: hung, and the chassis is a hazard. Middle: dressed and ready. High: ready, Price blunted a step.
Chassis Dressing.expires: When it is inhabited, or when the glyphs spoil. Bricking the chassis ends it.

Bridge Thin-Path.story: Two deep nodes, one night, and a crossing that feels like being a packet that half made it.
Bridge Thin-Path.plain: One crew crossing between two known deep nodes or Wired thin places.
Bridge Thin-Path.magnitude: Magnitude 3, the same as the Veil Thin-Path, and it needs a sanctum rated 3.
Bridge Thin-Path.scope: Wire Threshold. Both anchors must be nodes you know. The district's Overlay notices, and corps hate this specifically.
Bridge Thin-Path.seal: A night's work. Low: hung — you do not cross, or you cross badly. Middle: the bridge opens. High: it opens and Price is blunted a step.
Bridge Thin-Path.expires: It collapses as soon as the crew is through. Collapsing either node anchor, or an ICE storm, ends it early.

Scrub the Ghost-Code.story: Line by line, for hours, with the patient awake. Some of what you are deleting argues back.
Scrub the Ghost-Code.plain: Strips a corrupted Overlay mark, a hung daemon, or a rival's glyph. It cleans decks, nodes, and people with code under their skin.
Scrub the Ghost-Code.magnitude: This card's Magnitude must be equal to or greater than the stain. Your copy is written at one Magnitude between 1 and 5, and that is the ceiling on what it can clean.
Scrub the Ghost-Code.scope: Wire stains. The Veil cousin is Scrub the Stain.
Scrub the Ghost-Code.seal: An evening or a night by Magnitude. Low: partial — one clock step. Middle: the stain is gone. High: gone, and Price blunted a step.
Scrub the Ghost-Code.expires: Instantly at a successful sealing. Nothing is left standing; a rival can always re-infect.
